## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #13815: nested PowerShell script preservation — unwrap redundant nested `powershell -Command "..."` invocations (MODERATE priority, bash tool improvement)

- **What**: Cline's bash tool now detects redundant nested `powershell`/`pwsh` wrappers (e.g. `powershell -Command "Get-ChildItem | Where-Object { $_.Name -like '*.ts' }"`) and runs the decoded script directly through the existing UTF-8 stdin bootstrap, so `$_` variables and embedded quotes survive to the intended script. Previously a nested `powershell -Command "..."` had its double-quoted argument parsed by the outer PowerShell bootstrap: `$_` was interpolated away (expanded to empty string) before the nested shell ever saw it, so pipelines like `Get-ChildItem | Where-Object { $_.Name ... }` errored once per enumerated item (an error flood over large trees that looked like a hang) while the nested child still exited 0 (successful invocation with failed pipeline items). The unwrapping logic recognizes standalone `powershell`/`pwsh` with `-NoProfile`, optional `-NoLogo`/`-NonInteractive`, and exactly one ASCII single- or double-quoted `-Command` body, then decodes the script text and runs it through the existing UTF-8 stdin bootstrap. Quoted executable names (`&"C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe"`) are supported. Other flags, dynamic paths, here-string wrappers, and additional outer statements pass through unchanged (fall back to legacy native-argument escapes).
- **Why**: Nested PowerShell invocations lose variables (`$_`, `$PSItem`) and embedded quotes before the intended script runs, causing silent data-loss bugs (pipeline filters that always fail) or noisy error floods (one error per item, making it look like the command hung). Users and models may nest PowerShell for environment isolation, profile bypass, or edition switching (Windows PowerShell outer, PowerShell 7 inner). Without unwrapping, the inner script sees corrupted text instead of the intended source. The fix preserves the script text across editions (5.1 and 7) without changing process cancellation or output handling.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13815 (fix(shared): preserve nested PowerShell scripts across editions)
- **Category**: tool (bash, PowerShell invocation)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, ~3h. Alexi's bash tool (src/tool/tools/bash.ts) uses the same UTF-8 stdin bootstrap pattern for PowerShell commands (ported from Kilocode/Cline) but does NOT unwrap nested invocations. A user or model that wraps PowerShell in PowerShell (e.g. `powershell -Command "pwsh -Command 'Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.CPU -gt 10 }'"`) will hit the same interpolation bug. Port Cline's unwrapping logic: add a `getShellInvocation` helper (or equivalent) that detects standalone `powershell`/`pwsh` executables with `-NoProfile` and one ASCII single- or double-quoted `-Command` body, decodes the script text (strip the outer quotes, unescape inner quotes), and returns the decoded script + the requested executable (preserving the edition choice: `powershell` vs `pwsh`). Wire this into the bash tool's PowerShell execution path so the bootstrap receives the unwrapped script. Test on Windows: run `ax chat -m "run: powershell -Command \"Get-ChildItem | Where-Object { $_.Name -like '*.ts' }\""` and confirm the pipeline succeeds without errors (no "The property 'Name' cannot be found on this object" flood). Also test single-quoted `-Command 'Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.CPU -gt 10 }'` and verify `$_` is preserved. Verify cancellation still works (Ctrl+C mid-script) and that non-matching invocations (e.g. `powershell -File script.ps1`) pass through unchanged.

#### 2. Kilocode #13990: board_post recipient state warning — add targeted board posting with execution-state feedback (SMALL priority, new tool)

- **What**: Kilocode's `board_post` tool now returns `availability.recipientState` (completed/failed/cancelled/active/unknown) for direct-target posts and warns when the recipient has already stopped, so a parent agent does not wait on or resume a child merely to deliver a note that will never be read. Previously a parent could post a board message to a task child that had already finished, and the only feedback was an aggregate availability count and a generic "finished invocations" warning that grouped completed, failed, and cancelled recipients together. The new tool surfaces the observed recipient execution state at the point where the mistaken action happens: if the target is stopped, the result includes an explicit warning ("Recipient has already stopped; message stored but no reply should be expected") and the parent knows not to resume the child or wait for a reply. Broadcast posts, Task execution, and Agent Manager/user prompt queues are unchanged — only direct-target `board_post` gets the recipient-state feedback.
- **Why**: In Kilo Swarm (multi-agent coordination), a parent agent can post a board message to a task child that has already finished and continue to assume the child is still running. Task completion and board delivery are separate channels, so the message is stored but the child never reads it (it has already exited). Without explicit recipient-state feedback, the parent may wait indefinitely for a reply or waste a resume/restart cycle just to deliver a stale note. Direct-target posts with execution-state feedback reduce unnecessary wait and resume attempts against finished children, making swarm coordination more efficient and less error-prone.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13990 (fix(cli): warn when board_post targets a stopped subagent)
- **Category**: tool (board, swarm coordination)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~2h. Alexi has `kilo_board_read` and `kilo_board_write` (src/tool/tools/board.ts) but NO `board_post` tool — agents can broadcast to the whole board (`board_write` posts to the board without a target) but cannot target a specific subagent. Add a `kilo_board_post` tool with a `recipient` parameter (session ID or agent name) and return the recipient's execution state in the result. Schema: `{ recipient: string, content: string }`. Look up the recipient session via SessionManager (src/core/sessionManager.ts), check its status (running/completed/failed/cancelled/unknown), and include that in the result: `{ messageId: string, boardId: string, availability: { recipientState: 'completed' | 'failed' | 'cancelled' | 'active' | 'unknown' } }`. If the recipient is stopped (completed/failed/cancelled), add a warning to the result text or hint: "Recipient has already stopped; message stored but no reply should be expected. Do not resume the recipient just to deliver this note." If the recipient is active, return state without a warning. Test by creating a swarm with one child that completes (e.g. `task` tool with a short prompt that finishes immediately), then having the parent post to that child's session ID — confirm the warning appears, the state is `completed`, and the parent does not resume the child. Also test posting to an active child and verify no warning appears.

#### 3. OpenCode #48270: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model — add to SAP AI Core model catalog (SMALL priority, model catalog update)

- **What**: OpenCode's Go client added `deepseek-v4.1-flash` to its model catalog. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is a new fast, low-cost reasoning model variant in the DeepSeek V4 family (released late 2026-09). It supports the same reasoning API as `deepseek-v4-chat` (effort levels: low/medium/high, `reasoning_effort` field) but with a smaller context window and faster response time, optimized for simple tasks and high-throughput use cases.
- **Why**: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash offers a cheaper, faster alternative to the full V4 model for simple reasoning tasks (code review, error diagnosis, unit test generation). Alexi's DeepSeek provider (src/providers/deepseek.ts) and reasoning module (src/providers/reasoning.ts) already support DeepSeek reasoning models (effort normalization, `reasoning_effort` field, adaptive thinking), but the V4.1 Flash variant is not yet in the SAP AI Core model catalog refresh logic. Without the catalog entry, users cannot select `deepseek-v4.1-flash` via `--model` or routing config, even if SAP AI Core has deployed the model.
- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/48270 (feat(go): add DeepSeek V4.1 Flash)
- **Category**: provider (model catalog, DeepSeek)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~1h. Alexi's model catalog refresh (src/providers/modelCatalog.ts, `refreshModelCatalog`) fetches live deployments from SAP AI Core and merges them with static `ORCHESTRATION_MODELS`. Add `deepseek-v4.1-flash` to the static model list with the same reasoning capability profile as `deepseek-v4-chat` (reasoning: `levels`, budget: `reasoning_effort`, context: 32k or whatever SAP AI Core publishes). The model already matches the `deepseek-` prefix in src/providers/index.ts (`isOrchestrationModel`), so routing and provider dispatch require no changes. Test by running `ax chat --model deepseek-v4.1-flash -m "test"` and confirming the request succeeds (requires SAP AI Core to have deployed the model; mock test if the deployment is unavailable). Verify reasoning works: `ax chat --model deepseek-v4.1-flash --reasoning-effort high -m "explain how bubble sort works"` should emit reasoning blocks in the response.

#### 4. Kilocode #13991: Agent Manager section header chevrons — align expanded/collapsed chevron weight and remove aria-expanded highlight (LOW priority, VS Code UI-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode VS Code extension's Agent Manager section headers now render a single `chevron-right` glyph and rotate it 90 degrees for the expanded state, so both states share one path and weight. Previously the expanded and collapsed states used separate `chevron-down` and `chevron-right` icons that drew at different weights, so the expanded arrow looked larger and heavier than the collapsed one. The fix also removes the persistent background highlight from expanded sections: `aria-expanded="true"` is a semantic disclosure attribute that should not imply a visual active state, so the ghost-button active rule now keys only off explicit `data-expanded`, `data-active`, and `data-selected` attributes.
- **Why**: Inconsistent chevron weights and persistent highlights on expanded sections look unpolished (expanded sections had a blue background block and a heavier down chevron; collapsed sections stayed flat with a lighter chevron). The fix makes both states visually identical except for rotation, with a background only on hover. Intentional highlights (Agent Manager tab bar, active toggles) still use the explicit `data-active` attribute and are unaffected.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13991 (fix(vscode): align Agent Manager section header chevrons)
- **Category**: command (VS Code UI, icon styling)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no VS Code extension, no Agent Manager UI, no Electron desktop app. This is Kilocode/Cline desktop-specific. Not CLI-portable.

#### 5. Kilocode #13987: tool reveal replay and encrypted reasoning settlement — stop worktree-switch reveal animation and settle reasoning summaries earlier (LOW priority, VS Code UI-specific)

- **What**: Two Kilocode VS Code transcript rendering fixes: (1) Switching Agent Manager worktrees or sessions no longer replays the reveal animation of the last still-running tool (the card was growing from zero height again and shifting the layout on every switch). (2) Encrypted reasoning summaries (OpenAI Responses with `store: false`, used by the GPT-5 family through the Kilo gateway) now settle as done when a later part exists in the message or when the message is complete, instead of waiting for `time.end` (which arrives 5-30 seconds late because the encrypted continuation state only arrives on `output_item.done`). The `useGrowIn` wrapper now excludes tool parts (which keep their original status-gated `animate` and `reveal` behavior) and reasoning blocks (which have their own height and streaming animations). This restores pre-regression behavior for tools and fixes the 6px side clipping reported in #13974 for reasoning.
- **Why**: Worktree and session switches remount the transcript, so an already-seen live tool animated on every switch (layout jump, user confusion). Encrypted reasoning summaries kept their streaming state (pulsing header, streaming mask, follow-to-bottom) for 5-30 seconds after their text had stopped, so the turn status reflected a stale summary instead of the newest part (tool call or later reasoning summary). The fix makes transitions smooth without replay and without stale streaming states.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13987 (fix(vscode): stop tool reveal replay and settle encrypted reasoning)
- **Category**: command (VS Code UI, transcript rendering)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no VS Code extension, no Agent Manager worktrees, no desktop transcript UI. This is Kilocode/Cline desktop-specific. Not CLI-portable.

#### 8. OpenCode #48269: summarized adaptive thinking — request `display: "summarized"` for OpenAI Copilot (LOW priority, OpenAI Copilot-specific)

- **What**: OpenCode console now uses OpenAI Copilot's `adaptive_thinking` capability and always requests `display: "summarized"`, matching VS Code's behavior. Adaptive thinking is OpenAI's name for their extended reasoning feature (similar to Anthropic extended thinking, DeepSeek reasoning). The `display: "summarized"` option tells the API to return a summary of the reasoning trace instead of the full step-by-step trace, reducing response size and latency.
- **Why**: Without `display: "summarized"`, the full reasoning trace can be verbose (10x the summary size) and slow to transmit. VS Code's Copilot extension already uses summarized reasoning by default, so OpenCode console aligns with that behavior. Closes OpenCode issue #46593.
- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/48269 (fix(opencode): request summarized adaptive thinking)
- **Category**: provider (OpenAI Copilot, reasoning)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi does NOT use OpenAI Copilot (Alexi's providers are SAP AI Core Orchestration, with optional OpenAI/GitLab; no Copilot integration). This is OpenCode-console-specific. Not actionable. If Alexi adds Copilot support in the future, remember to request `display: "summarized"` for adaptive thinking to reduce response size.
